intro:
This morning, it was time to say goodbye to Brescia, and I have to admit, I felt a little sadness leaving. After spending so much time here, it had started to feel like a home away from home. I’ve really enjoyed my time in Brescia, and leaving was harder than I expected. But the long way around continues, and today would take me on quite a journey!

As I headed south, the landscape was still a little hazy. In the distance, I could make out the snow-capped Alps, almost hiding behind the haze. Eventually, as I continued toward Genoa, the mountains gave way to rolling hills, and the scenery began to change.

And then, suddenly, there it was - the Ligurian Sea!

The water was a brilliant blue, unlike anything I had seen before. Being colorblind, I don’t always experience colors the way others do, but this was different. The blue was so vivid, so striking, that I couldn’t help but notice it.

I’ve seen the ocean along both the East and West Coasts of the United States, and even spent time in Hawaii, but there was something about the water here that was unlike any of them. I can’t quite explain what made it so different. It was the color, the way the light caught the water, and perhaps the setting itself. Whatever it was, I was mesmerized.

Driving along the coast was incredible. The road twisted and turned high above the water, with the Ligurian Sea stretching out beside me. Around every bend seemed to be another breathtaking view. Every so often, I found myself simply looking over in awe, amazed by the beauty of it all.

After so many days surrounded by mountains, seeing that vast expanse of blue was something special. It was one of those unexpected moments when the journey itself becomes the highlight, and all you can do is take it in.

As I made my way into Monaco from the motorway, I was surprised by just how hilly the landscape was. I hadn’t expected that! The road was full of twists and turns as I worked my way down, and then suddenly, the view opened up before me. There it was - Monaco! Not just a city, but an entire country, seemingly laid out right in front of me.

It was beautiful. The hills rolled down toward the harbor, with buildings covering the slopes and the Mediterranean Sea stretching out beyond them. What amazed me most was the perspective. From where I was, it felt as though I could see the entire city and country in a single sweeping view.

I eventually made my way to a parking garage, got out, and took some pictures. I wanted to capture that incredible sight, the city nestled into the hills with the harbor below.

I’ve spent this trip driving across countries, sometimes for hours just to get from one place to another. Yet here I was, standing in Monaco, realizing that nearly an entire country could fit into one breathtaking panorama. It was such an unusual perspective, and one I won’t soon forget.

As I made my way back toward Genoa, I was treated to another beautiful sight. This time, it wasn’t just the Ligurian Sea that caught my attention, but the city of Genoa itself, nestled along the coastline with that incredible blue water stretching out beside it.

What a beautiful city! Seeing the buildings spread across the hillsides, with the sea as their backdrop, gave me an entirely different appreciation for the area. Earlier in the day, I had been so captivated by the water that I hadn’t really taken in the city itself. Now, seeing them together, I was amazed all over again.

Genoa was never meant to be a stop on this trip, just somewhere I would pass through on the way to Monaco. But after seeing it today, I know one thing for certain: I want to come back and spend some real time exploring this city. Some places leave an impression without you ever setting foot in them, and Genoa was definitely one of those places.

As I turned north in the afternoon, the scenery began changing once again, and I found myself completely captivated by the Alps. The snow-capped mountains were simply a thing of beauty, rising above the valleys as I made my way toward Courmayeur.

I noticed on my map that the Matterhorn was somewhere behind the mountains ahead of me. It almost became a game of hide-and-seek. At one point, I thought I could see its famous peak poking out from behind the others, but just as quickly, the surrounding mountains seemed to swallow it up again. It was as though the Matterhorn was determined to remain a mystery!

As I continued through the Aosta Valley, the sun was beginning to set, and the mountains put on one final display. The last rays of sunlight touched only the very tops of the peaks, illuminating them for a few precious moments before slowly fading away.

But something I’ve come to appreciate about the mountains is how different twilight feels here. Even after the sun has disappeared, the sky holds on to its light, and the silhouettes of the mountains remain visible against it. There’s a quiet beauty to that time of evening, when the sunlight is gone but the mountains haven’t yet disappeared into the darkness.

Another fascinating sight caught my attention along the way. Just before entering one of the tunnels, I happened to look up and spotted what appeared to be the Château de Saint-Germain, perched high on the mountainside. There it stood, seemingly all alone, overlooking the valley below. And as I continued driving, I began noticing what looked like other castles and old structures scattered across the surrounding hills.

It amazed me to think about how long these places have stood there, watching over the valleys and the generations of travelers who have passed through. Here I was, driving through modern tunnels beneath mountains crowned with centuries of history. The Aosta Valley is truly an interesting place!

By the time I finally reached my hotel in Courmayeur, I was running dangerously low on fuel. After 837 kilometers of driving, I was certainly ready to call it a day! Thankfully, my accommodations for the next two nights have a washer and dryer, so part of my evening was dedicated to the less glamorous side of traveling - laundry!

I managed to sneak down to the tiny bistro associated with the hotel for dinner, where I enjoyed a delicious plate of gnocchi followed by yet another homemade tiramisu. And it was amazing! Italy continues to spoil me when it comes to food.

But the day had one final surprise waiting.

Before going to bed, I stepped out onto the balcony. Everything around me was dark, with the mountains and surrounding landscape almost completely swallowed by the night. Above me, however, the stars were shining.

At first, I could make out what seemed like only a handful of stars scattered across the sky. But when I pointed my phone’s night camera upward, an entirely different picture emerged. Suddenly, there were so many more stars than my eyes could see! It was incredible to discover just how much was hiding in that darkness.

What a remarkable way to end the day. From the brilliant blue waters of the Ligurian Sea to the snow-capped Alps glowing in the last light of sunset, and finally to a sky filled with stars, today was another reminder of just how much beauty there is to discover along the long way around.
